title: The Death of the Earl of Chatham (The Collapse of the Earl of Chatham in the House of Lords, 7 July 1778)

source.label: Wikipedia: “he moved to London in 1774, never returning to America”
Wikipedia: “a key work in establishing Copley's reputation as a history painter”

work.text: But the artist's fame as a historical painter was made by The Death of the Earl of Chatham showing the collapse in the House of Lords of the former Prime Minister William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham.
He had especial felicity in seizing upon the incident of the day for the exercise of his pencil

source.author: Martha Babcock Amory
source.title: The Domestic and Artistic Life of John Singleton Copley, R.A.

moment.text: the vast number of noble heads, all portraits, with which the house of lords is thronged ; its chief fault is an air of formality, and a deficiency of deep feeling … All lords could not feel alike ; — some seem standing for their portraits ; some seem anxious about their places

source.author: Allan Cunningham
source.title: Lives of the Most Eminent British Painters (1829–33), as quoted in William Dunlap, A History of the Rise and Progress of the Arts of Design in the United States (1834)

moment.text: Copley rented out a private room to exhibit the painting, charging for admission. He also made money from the painting from prints of it, marketed by John Boydell.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors
source.title: The Death of the Earl of Chatham

moment.text: In an open letter Chambers accused Copley of purveying his picture like a "raree-show" and of aiming for "either the sale of prints or the raffle of the picture."
moment.lead: The Royal Academy’s Sir William Chambers objected:

matters.text: It depicts the collapse of William Pitt, 1st Earl of Chatham on 7 April 1778, during a debate in the House of Lords on the American War of Independence.

source.author: Wikipedia contributors

matters.text: The picture called the Death of Lord Chatham, is connected with the history of America.
